description.value: The study examined serum neurofilament light chain levels in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration according to C9orf72 repeat expansion status and clinical phenotype, and assessed associations with brain atrophy rates and survival time.

spans.text: The aim of the present study was to compare the levels of serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) in frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) patients of different clinical subtypes (bvFTD, PPA, and FTLD‐MND) and with or without the   C9orf72   repeat expansion, and to correlate sNfL levels to disease progression, assessed by the brain atrophy rate and survival time.

description.value: The study was conducted and patients were recruited at Kuopio University Hospital, Finland.

definition.value: correlation between sNfL levels and brain atrophy rates

spans.text: Longitudinal data from repeated scans were available for 11 patients.
The overall cortical atrophy rate was found to significantly correlate with elevated sNfL levels (R  = −0.64,   P   = 0.018).

value: The overall cortical atrophy rate significantly correlated with elevated sNfL levels, including frontal lobe atrophy rate. There were also significant correlations between sNfL levels and atrophy rates of the thalamus, caudate, pallidum, putamen, and overall subcortical grey matter.

spans.text: The overall cortical atrophy rate was found to significantly correlate with elevated sNfL levels (R  = −0.64,   P   = 0.018). Of separate brain lobes, only frontal lobe atrophy rate was observed to correlate with a higher sNfL concentration (R  = −0.72,   P   = 0.006). Furthermore, when correlating subcortical grey matter structures, there was a significant correlation between sNfL levels and the atrophy rate of the thalamus (R  = −0.61,   P   = 0.024), caudate (R  = −0.62,   P   = 0.022), pallidum (R  = −0.73,   P   = 0.005), and putamen (R  = −0.70,   P   = 0.008). Also, atrophy of the overall subcortical grey matter correlated with sNfL levels (R =−0.68,   P   = 0.011).
